text.p: - Slovenian parliament on Wednesday passed a law freezing salaries of parliamentary members and other top state officials.
- Ministry of Finance postponed raising car insurance policies by 35 percent for drivers under 25 years of age, but said it would lift prices by about 20 percent for all drivers regardless of age.
- Power plants on the river Drava will buy nine turbines from troubled metal company Litostroj; each turbine costs 5.2 million marks ($3.08 million).
- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek and parliamentary president Janez Podobnik met the new arch-bishop Franc Rode on Wednesday.
- Petrol distribution and trading companies complained that the last nine percent increase in petrol prices is giving them only 1.7 percent, while the rest goes into Slovenia's budget.
- Hotels in coastal Portoroz invested some 900 million tolars ($5.8 million) in the last three months for reconstruction of its facilities.
- Slovenia still has some 8,350 refugees from the former Yugoslavia, of which 5,000 are still unable to return home.
- Turkish president Suleyman Demirel will make a two-day official visit to Slovenia on April 3.
- Slovenian Privatisation Agency said that 952 companies have already completed privatisation, while another 1,363 companies are still in the process.
